ENGLISH LANGUAGE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #15
====

GRADE: Grade 6
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Writing 1.4.1 Guided Writing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.4.1 Guided Writing.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.4.1 Guided Writing.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.4.1 Guided Writing.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.4.1 Guided Writing.

2. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the Library
   B. Where is the library
   C. Where is the library?
   D. where is the library

3. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only a describing word
   B. Only an action
   C. A person, place, thing, or idea
   D. Only a joining word

4. When practising Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.

5. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Listening Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Listening Comprehension.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Listening Comprehension.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Listening Comprehension.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Listening Comprehension.

6. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.

7. When practising Pronunciation and Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Pronunciation and Listening.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pronunciation and Listening.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Pronunciation and Listening.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Pronunciation and Listening.

8. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. goes
   B. goed
   C. went
   D. going

9. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Listening.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Listening.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Listening.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Listening.

10. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. Many unrelated topics with no link
   B. One main idea with supporting sentences
   C. No full stops
   D. Only one word repeated

11. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. run
   B. quickly
   C. happiness
   D. blue

12. When practising Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Writing 12.4.1 Functional Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 13.1.1 Pronunciation and Intensive Listening and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Pronunciation and Intensive Listening and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 13.2.1 Extensive Reading and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

====

1. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.4.1 Guided Writing.

2. C — Where is the library?

3. C — A person, place, thing, or idea

4. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.

5. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Listening Comprehension.

6. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.

7. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pronunciation and Listening.

8. C — went

9. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Listening.

10. B — One main idea with supporting sentences

11. A — run

12. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Writing 12.4.1 Functional Writing; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Listening and Speaking 13.1.1 Pronunciation and Intensive Listening; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Pronunciation and Intensive Listening; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reading 13.2.1 Extensive Reading; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
